authority: #K2-454 sec.2.5 gate: the conditional N=1 may only run if the IN-BAND PRECHECK shows a significant drop in the no-free-start-node blocks relative to the 281 failures. This is that measurement: a --dry-run of the SAME wrapper on the SAME wiped board with the SAME channels/guide (no board written, no grading).

inputs.channels_args: identical to the R1430 run (hard n_nets=18 + soft n_guide=48, guide_source=joint-per-corridor)
inputs.note: a dry-run stops after the ledger is written (k2_p4_mroute_v1.py:792) => no board, no grading, and it is the very instrument the ruling names.

gate_verdict.significant: YES - the class the ruling names collapses by 91%.

three_mechanism_findings: 245 of the former no-free-start-node blocks are, once expressed correctly (port <-> port), SAME-ISLAND NO-OPS: they never needed routing at all. They were pure noise that cost two doomed retry solves each - which is why the maze stage took ~31 min in R1430 and ~1 min now.

The remaining 23 are genuinely start-blocked: P3V3 x21, P3V3_AUX x2 (plus I2C2_SCL x1 which is the R1430 residual and fails with no-path-coarse(exhausted-5693) instead: a free-space disconnection, NOT a start problem).

Geometry is UNCHANGED where it matters: segs 636, vias 60, len 576.7708 - byte-identical to R1430. The only count change is added 68 -> 67, and that one is a PHANTOM: with the correct formulation it becomes a named no-op, i.e. the previous run counted an add that produced no copper (consistent with I2C1_SDA still being unconnected on the final board).
honest_scope: class A (both ends outside the wall) is fixed and the gate is met. It does NOT target the two R1430 residuals: I2C2_SCL is a free-space disconnection inside the frame, and I2C1_SDA is a drawing-side pair. So C1 may well stay 2 - the conditional run measures that, it does not promise a win.
